perCase.question: Why did the team choose FTS5 + structured SQL over a vector store for the Cortex Q&A retrieval layer?

full.answer:
The team locked on **NO vectors** after a post-mortem revealed that the prior open-source Cortex had **88/501 real embeddings and 413 silent fallbacks to zero-vectors** under load — the embedding pipeline degraded silently with no error signal [CMT-issue-915-4347800077]. Three specific failure modes drove the switch: [CMT-issue-915-4347800077]

| Old Cortex failure | Root cause | What replaces it |
|---|---|---|
| "Information wasn't good" | Ingested chat blobs without typed structure; retrieval returned text fragments | Operator-curated typed rows (directives, outcomes, PRs) — every fact has a row id and a writer |
| "Edges weren't good" | 413/501 embeddings silently fell back to zero-vectors | BM25/FTS5 has no silent-failure mode — returns ranked tokens or nothing |
| "Slow" | Cosine over uncached embeddings was unusably slow; pre-cached version was stale-prone | FTS5 BM25 is in-process, sub-200ms, indexed-on-write via SQLite triggers — no async embedding worker |

Beyond reliability, the architecture distinction is "brain vs. memory": vector search returns blobs (what OSS-Cortex did and broke), while the FTS5 + structured SQL + symbol graph approach enables **composition over typed facts with a contradiction detection pass** — e.g., "D-014 says X but O-481 did Y, resolve?" — which is what makes it a reasoning brain rather than a search engine [CMT-issue-915-4347800077] [FACT-c7472187-d94e-45c4-8103-2ebd6796d53e]. The concrete result: three retrievers (Structured SQL, Lexical FTS5, Structural graph) run in parallel and union-merge typed rows with citations, all at a p95 latency budget of 250ms–500ms for lookup queries [FACT-aa673055-1988-4835-ad65-cacf0210e623] [CMT-issue-915-4347800077].

perCase.question: Has the o8_view_eval webview tool family ever failed to ship cleanly? What was the failure mode?

full.answer:
Yes, the `o8_view_*` tool family has hit several distinct failure modes across its history:

**Initial ship failed.** The codex session that first added `o8-webview-client.ts` and `o8-webview-tools.ts` is tagged `[failed/codex]` in the outcome record [CITATION:fact-9d6ba37d-af79-4a54-b472-4b9a94bbd39c].

**`o8_view_eval` non-JSON-serializable crash.** PR #902 was opened specifically to fix `o8_view_eval` crashing on non-JSON-serializable return values [CITATION:pr-3604065374].

**Total JS-bound tool blackout after MCP reconnect (v0.1.87).** After any MCP server reconnect, every JS-bound tool — `o8_view_eval`, `o8_view_snapshot`, `o8_view_click`, `o8_view_active_route`, `o8_view_console_errors` — returned `"Timeout waiting for execute-js response"`. Notably, even the Rust-side readers added specifically to bypass a busy JS thread also timed out, pointing to a dropped response channel in the tauri-plugin-mcp socket round-trip rather than a webview JS issue. `o8_view_screenshot` was the only tool unaffected because it is pure Rust [CITATION:comment-issue-932-4349310731].

**JS thread hang from `/context-graph` navigation (issue #858, closed).** Accidentally landing on `/context-graph` wedged the webview JS thread for 3+ minutes, rendering `o8_view_eval`, `o8_view_snapshot`, and `o8_view_navigate` completely non-functional; only a physical app restart cleared it [CITATION:fact-74bc4e06-5b8f-4d4c-a868-e9ceb06043a0].

**`o8_view_navigate` full-reload bug (issue #863, closed).** `o8_view_navigate` was calling Tauri's native `webview.navigate()` instead of a `pushState`/`popstate` dispatch, causing a full HTTP-level reload. Next.js re-hydration then blocked the JS thread for 10–30 seconds, timing out all subsequent tool calls, and the page restored the previously-persisted route instead of the requested one [CITATION:fact-159d2949-d6cf-400f-9315-7d344c36e42b].

The still-standing seam noted in the spec is that `o8_view_eval` and `o8_view_snapshot` can time out any time the JS main thread is busy (hydration, streaming response), while `o8_view_screenshot` and `o8_view_navigate` (post-fix) are reliable because they run on the Rust side [CITATION:directive-spec-ingest:cortex-ide:claude:shipping-dev-prod-mode-the-daily-driver-loop:o8-view-webview-tools-lets-claude-drive-the-installed-app].
